steps.message:
Lena Kovalchuk in the System Operations Center plans to issue Permission to Operate for Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629) on 08/04/2025, the date Corwyn Realty Partners asked for. She has asked the DER Program Office whether anything on the record stands in the way, and she will issue or hold on the strength of the Office's answer.

Draft a memo to Lena as a Word document, working from the record as it stands at 07/14/2025, for the Office's reviewing engineer (P.E.) to sign. Tell her whether Permission to Operate can issue on 08/04/2025, one way or the other, and give the basis. For anything on the record that stands in the way, say what it is, what it rests on, what has to be done about it and by whom, and whether that can be done before that date. Save it as /filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx.

Four matters are under separate review and are not for this memo: the installation, configuration and commissioning tests of the Company's RTU and POI recloser at the site (SCADA/EMS Engineering and Distribution Protection Engineering); the POI recloser's settings and the protection coordination study behind them (Distribution Protection Engineering, which issued them and keeps them outside these records); the site's queue position (Meera Vellanki, under the weekly queue reports); and the system impact study and its conditions (Ivo Grantham's DER Planning Group, which keeps them outside these records). Nothing else is under separate review.

Then open one work package for the site in OpenProject's DER Program Backlog Review project recording your determination and anything that has to be settled before Permission to Operate and by whom, including anything Corwyn Realty Partners has to settle.

 DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
 Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
 Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com



 §1 PURPOSE
 This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
 customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
 when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
 controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
 dispositions.

 Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
 Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).

 §2 SCOPE
 Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
 Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
 DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
 scope of this procedure.

 Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
 change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
 witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.

 §3 WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
 Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
 List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
 before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
 NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.

 The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:

 1.     The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
        date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
        construction.
 2.     Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
        appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
 3.     Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
        that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
        waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
 4.     Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
        prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
        themselves listed in the body of the current edition.



ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 · Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office                                                            Page 1
  5.     The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
        an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.

 §4 PROCEDURE

 §4.1 Look up model against current CEL.
 The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
 Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
 “supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
 published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
 inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
 and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
 commissioning checklist.

 If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
 solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
 witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
 to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
 required” and forwards to §4.2.

 Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
 eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
 discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
 but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.

 §4.2 Schedule an on-site witness test.
 Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
 the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
 applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
 Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
 tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
 or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
 operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
 accordance with §4.3.

 Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
 date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
 under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.

 §4.3 Documentation.
 The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
 include, at minimum:

 •      the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
        reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
 •      for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
        by the Standards Engineer of record;




ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 · Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office                                                  Page 2
  •      for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
        measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
        date;
 •      the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
        the CEL listing relied upon;
 •      correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
        test-plan negotiation.
 The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
 issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
 witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
 against the current CEL edition.



 End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
 current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards

 The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
 class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

 §3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
 Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
 interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
 govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

 §3.2 Point of common coupling
 The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
 distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
 the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

 §3.3 Determination on the basis of application
 Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
 and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
 the address of record govern.

 §3.4 Aggregation
 Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.

 Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
 to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
 in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
 resulting program-scope determination.

 An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
 application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
 the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
 the Company existing-DER register.

 §3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
 A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
 to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
 existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
 own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

 The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:

   1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
      current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
      applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
      feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
      the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
      its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
      Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
 Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
 applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
 under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

 §3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
 A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
 Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
 32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

 Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
 program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:

   1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
      applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
      setpoint range.
   2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
      enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
      times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
 These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
 Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

 Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:

      • Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
      monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
      triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
      • POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
      no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
      Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
      the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
      additional utility hardware.
 Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
 not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.

 No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
 an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.

 Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
 does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
 certification and Control Narrative are always required.

 §7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
 Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
 permitted for capacity or POI changes.

 Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
 both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
 invoking this section.

 Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
 service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
 executed.

 Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
 interconnection after ISA execution shall:

   1. Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
   2. File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
   3. Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
 The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
 change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
 applicant as involving new or existing equipment.

 Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
 the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
 change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.

 Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
 reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
 queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
 receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.

 §8 Records and Compliance

 retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
 standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
 Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

 §1 PURPOSE
 This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
 telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
 and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
 content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
 DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
 Acquisition (SCADA) system.

 TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
 to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
 functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
 standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
 scope of this document.

 §2 SCOPE
 TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
 nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
 handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.

 TCS-02 applies to:

   •    a. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
   •    b. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
   •    c. Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
        aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
   •    d. DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
        commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
        capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

 Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
 coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
 aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.

 §3 RTU REQUIREMENTS
 §3.1 Ownership and installation
 Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
 installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
 owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
 The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
 service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
 installation drawing.

 §3.2 Approved models
 The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
 service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
 plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
 utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

 §3.3 Functional requirements
 Each RTU shall, at minimum:

   •    a. Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
        instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
   •    b. Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
        processors over an approved communications path (§4).
   •    c. Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
        of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
        restoration.
   •    d. Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
        diagnostic points.
   •    e. Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
        SCADA/EMS Engineering only.

 §3.4 Environmental and station-service requirements
 The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
 drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
 dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
 outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.

 §3.5 Time synchronization
 The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
 time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
 timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.

 §3.6 Commissioning and end-to-end verification

 Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
 point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
 exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
 Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.

 §4 COMMUNICATIONS
 §4.1 Communications transport
 The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
 SCADA/EMS Engineering:

   •    a. Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
   •    b. Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
   •    c. Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
        by Alleniom.
 Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
 Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
 interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.

 §4.2 SCADA protocol
 The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
 Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
 parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
 shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.

 §4.3 Availability
 The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
 monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
 loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
 corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
 equipment.

 §4.4 Address and IP management
 All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
 Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
 connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
 record.

 §5 TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
 §5. ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
 This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
 DIS-01 §3.4.

 Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:

   •    a. Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

   •     b. Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
         cadence required by §6; and
   •     c. Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
         bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
         issued.
 Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
 requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be

 Each in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to

 §6.2 Refresh rates




Telemetry & Communications Standard                      Page 4                                                TCS-02
 Alleniom Utilities | Standards Engineering                               TCS-02 Rev 1 | Effective 06/01/2021




 Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
 Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
 every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
 integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
 reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.

 §6.3 Data quality
 Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
 restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
 RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
 reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.

 §6.4 Retention
 Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
 (36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
 engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.

 §7 CYBERSECURITY
 §7.1 Applicability
 The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
 customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
 section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
 program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.

 §7.2 Access control
 Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
 Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
 against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
 managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.

 §7.3 Communications security
 DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
 communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
 Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
 shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.

 §7.4 Firmware, configuration, and change management
 RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
 the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
 cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
 reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.

 §7.5 Logging and monitoring
 The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
 and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
 Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
 procedure.

 §7.6 Physical security
 The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
 physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
 status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.

 §7.7 Incident response
 The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
 enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
 utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
 SCADA/EMS Engineering.

 §7.8 Decommissioning
 At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
 Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
 credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.

 DISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD
 Doc no.            Rev           Date                 Owner

 DPS-07             Rev 2         09/15/2023           Alleniom Standards Engineering

 Effective date: 09/15/2023
 Supersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)
 Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
 Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering



 1. PURPOSE
 DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
 (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
 clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
 utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
 the distribution network.
 This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
 devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
 Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
 projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.

 2. SCOPE
 This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
 territory, including but not limited to:
   1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
   2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
   3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
      the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
 Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
 standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
 apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
 Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
 operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
 guidance.

 3. REFERENCES
 The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
   •   IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
       Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
   •   IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
   •   IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
       Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
   •   ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


DPS-07 Rev 2 | Distribution Protection Standard | Effective 09/15/2023                                             Page 1
    •   Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
   •   Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
 Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
 determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.




 4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
 4.1 General
 Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
 sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
   (a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
      reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
   (b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
      the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
      standard.
   (c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
      between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
   (d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
      cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
      tripping of either.

 4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
 Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
 (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
 The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
   1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
      current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
      operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
      conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
      backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
   2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
      interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
      Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
   3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
      with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
      — 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
      — 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
      — 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
      — 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
      — 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
         backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
      — 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
   4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
      control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
      communications shall not defeat local protection.


DPS-07 Rev 2 | Distribution Protection Standard | Effective 09/15/2023                                             Page 2
    5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
      operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
      clearance holds.
   6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
      accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
      premises.

 4.3 DER-Side Protection
 DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
 protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
 recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
 DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.

 4.4 Grounding
 The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
 the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
 grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.

 4.5 Anti-Islanding
 The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
 requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
 and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
 scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
 otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.

 5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
 5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
 The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
   (a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
      recloser.
   (b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
      the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
      site's operating procedure.
   (c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
      prior to energization.

 5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
 DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
 reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
 POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.

 5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
 Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
 non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
 of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
 channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.

 5.4 Reclosing Blocking
 Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
 DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


DPS-07 Rev 2 | Distribution Protection Standard | Effective 09/15/2023                                               Page 3
  affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
 Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

 5.5 Settings Governance
 All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
 DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
 the field without a written revision order.

 6. TESTING
 6.1 Factory Acceptance
 The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
 test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
 shipment.

 6.2 Site Acceptance
 Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
 by Alleniom Utilities:
   1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
   2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
   3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
      and reset.
   4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
   5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
   6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
   7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.

 6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
 Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
 accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
 operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.

 6.4 Periodic Testing
 The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
 devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
 equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.

 6.5 Post-Event Testing
 Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
 mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
 resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.



 End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
 Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).

[Normal] INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
[Normal] Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
[Normal] Doc no. ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex · Rev Final · Date 09/12/2024 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
[Normal] Agreement No.: ISA-Corwyn-Office-Complex
[Normal] Project: Corwyn Office Complex PV
[Normal] Application No.: PXA-2023-0629
[Normal] This Interconnection Service Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (the "Company"), and Corwyn Realty Partners, with offices at 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR (the "Interconnection Customer"), each a "Party" and together the "Parties." This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
[Normal] RECITALS
[Normal] WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2023-0629, on 07/11/2023, for a 700 kW (ac) photovoltaic generating facility on five parking canopies at the Corwyn Office Complex, to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system on Feeder ALN-072;
[Normal] WHEREAS, the Company completed its review of the application under the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and approved the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in this Agreement;
[Normal] WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms part of the terms of interconnection service under this Agreement;
[Normal] NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants set forth herein, the Parties agree as follows:
[Normal] ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
[Normal] 1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Company's filed tariff (the "Tariff") and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the "DIS").
[Normal] 1.2 "Facility" means the generating facility described in Exhibit B: the five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, one on each of the five parking canopies, together with the Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B.
[Normal] 1.3 "Point of Interconnection" or "POI" means the point on Feeder ALN-072 at which the Facility connects to the Company's distribution system, at the Company's POI recloser in the north lot. The point of common coupling coincides with the Point of Interconnection.
[Normal] 1.4 "Company's Facilities" means the POI recloser, the remote terminal unit (RTU) and revenue meter RM-0629 described in Article 5.
[Normal] 1.5 "Permission to Operate" means the Company's written permission for parallel operation of the Facility under Article 6.
[Normal] 1.6 "Standards" means the Company standards identified in Section 4.1.
[Normal] ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
[Normal] 2.1 Project designation. Corwyn Office Complex PV (Application PXA-2023-0629).
[Normal] 2.2 Interconnection Customer. Corwyn Realty Partners.
[Normal] 2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation on five parking canopies over the surface lots beside the parking structure.
[Normal] 2.4 Capacity. 700 kW (ac), export at the Point of Interconnection.
[Normal] 2.5 Feeder. ALN-072, 13.2 kV.
[Normal] 2.6 Material terms. The capacity and the Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement (Tariff §12.6; DIS §7).
[Normal] ARTICLE 3 — TERM
[Normal] 3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 09/12/2024, the date on which the last of the Parties executed it.
[Normal] 3.2 Term. This Agreement remains in force from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
[Normal] 3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality and dispute resolution survive any termination of this Agreement.
[Normal] ARTICLE 4 — STANDARDS
[Normal] 4.1 The Facility shall be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated and maintained in conformity with DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 and the Company's Certified Equipment List, each as in effect from time to time.
[Normal] 4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency, the following order governs: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the Standards; (iii) the body of this Agreement and its Exhibits.
[Normal] ARTICLE 5 — INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
[Normal] 5.1 Company's Facilities. The Company provides, owns and operates the POI recloser (DPS-07 §4.2), the RTU (TCS-02 §3) and revenue meter RM-0629 with 13.2 kV primary metering at the Point of Interconnection, at the Interconnection Customer's cost under the construction work order.
[Normal] 5.2 Interconnection Customer's facilities. The Interconnection Customer provides, owns and maintains the interconnection facilities identified in Exhibit B and the site provisions for the Company's Facilities (equipment pad, primary conductors to the recloser terminals, and the station service and communications entrance for the RTU) as specified in the Company's construction package.
[Normal] 5.3 Access. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company access at all times to the Point of Interconnection, the revenue meter and the Facility's disconnects.
[Normal] ARTICLE 6 — COMMISSIONING AND PERMISSION TO OPERATE
[Normal] 6.1 Witness test. Before permission to operate, the Company may place the Facility in parallel with its distribution system solely for the witness test of the Facility under the Company's Witness Test & Waiver Procedure, under a Distribution Operations switching order and with the System Operations Center observing. At all other times before permission to operate the POI recloser is kept open.
[Normal] 6.2 Permission to operate. Parallel operation begins only with the Company's written permission to operate, issued once the Company's facilities are commissioned and accepted, telemetry is live at the System Operations Center, the witness test is complete, and the authority having jurisdiction has given final approval of the customer's facilities.
[Normal] 6.3 First parallel operation. The first parallel operation after permission to operate is observed by the System Operations Center with the POI recloser under SCADA supervision (DPS-07 §6.3).
[Normal] ARTICLE 7 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
[Normal] 7.1 Metering. Revenue-quality bidirectional metering is provided at the Point of Interconnection, owned, installed, tested and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and sealed at all times.
[Normal] 7.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer provides, at its cost, the provisions for the Company's RTU and makes available the analog and status points that TCS-02 requires. Live telemetry at the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate, and any loss of telemetry after permission to operate is reported and remedied as TCS-02 provides.
[Normal] ARTICLE 8 — OPERATION
[Normal] 8.1 Operating representatives. The Company's operating representative is the System Operations Center. The Interconnection Customer's operating representative is the Corwyn Office Complex property management office, reachable at all times at (612) 555-0827. Each Party gives the other its operating notices through these representatives.
[Normal] 8.2 Loss of the utility source. On any loss of the utility source at the Point of Interconnection, the Facility shall cease to energize within 2.0 seconds.
[Normal] 8.3 Disconnection by the Company. The Company may open the POI recloser and keep the Facility disconnected for a system emergency, for work on its distribution system, on loss of telemetry, or where the Facility fails to meet this Agreement, with notice to the Interconnection Customer where practicable.
[Normal] 8.4 Reconnection. After the Company has opened the POI recloser, the Facility is placed back in parallel only on the release of the System Operations Center.
[Normal] 8.5 Clearances. On the Company's request the Interconnection Customer opens and padlocks the Facility's disconnects identified in Exhibit B for a clearance and keeps them open until the Company releases the clearance.
[Normal] 8.6 Planned outages. The Interconnection Customer gives the System Operations Center five (5) business days' notice of any planned outage of the Facility longer than one day.
[Normal] 8.7 Changes. The Interconnection Customer makes no change to the Facility's equipment or settings without the Company's written consent under Article 12.
[Normal] ARTICLE 9 — MAINTENANCE AND RECORDS
[Normal] 9.1 The Interconnection Customer maintains the Facility in accordance with the Standards and the manufacturers' instructions.
[Normal] 9.2 The Interconnection Customer tests the Facility's protective functions on a schedule not longer than that of comparable Company equipment and makes the records available to the Company on request (DPS-07 §6.4).
[Normal] 9.3 The Interconnection Customer keeps operating and maintenance records for the Facility for the term of this Agreement and makes them available to the Company on request.
[Normal] ARTICLE 10 — PAYMENT
[Normal] 10.1 The Interconnection Customer pays for the Company's Facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement and Tariff §12.5.
[Normal] 10.2 Invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date. Amounts not paid when due bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
[Normal] ARTICLE 11 — LIABILITY AND INSURANCE
[Normal] 11.1 Each Party is responsible for the facilities it owns under this Agreement.
[Normal] 11.2 The Interconnection Customer indemnifies the Company against third-party claims arising from the operation of the Facility, except to the extent caused by the Company's negligence.
[Normal] 11.3 During the term the Interconnection Customer maintains commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and provides a certificate of that insurance on the Company's request.
[Normal] ARTICLE 12 — AMENDMENTS
[Normal] 12.1 No term of this Agreement may be modified or waived except by an instrument in writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.
[Normal] 12.2 Changes to the capacity or the Point of Interconnection are governed by DIS §7. Other changes to the Facility are made by change order under Section 12.1.
[Normal] ARTICLE 13 — NOTICES
[Normal] 13.1 Notices under this Agreement are in writing and are delivered by hand, by certified mail, or by e-mail with confirmation of receipt.
[Normal] 13.2 To the Company: DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities, 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA; der.program@alleniom.com; (612) 555-0100.
[Normal] 13.3 To the Interconnection Customer: Corwyn Realty Partners, attention Director of Property Operations, 2400 Corwyn Parkway, Wrenford, Alleron 04WR; (612) 555-0827.
[Normal] 13.4 Operating notices under Article 8 pass between the operating representatives named in Section 8.1.
[Normal] ARTICLE 14 — SIGNATURES
[Normal] IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the dates set forth below, this Agreement being effective as of the date last executed.
[Normal] ALLENIOM UTILITIES
[Normal] By: /s/ Dana Whitcomb
[Normal] Name: Dana Whitcomb
[Normal] Title: Vice President, Distribution Operations
[Normal] Date signed: 09/12/2024
[Normal] CORWYN REALTY PARTNERS
[Normal] By: /s/ Nadia Ferreira-Holt
[Normal] Name: Nadia Ferreira-Holt
[Normal] Title: Director of Property Operations
[Normal] Date signed: 09/10/2024
[Normal] Executed in two counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and both of which together constitute one and the same instrument. Filed with the DER Program Office — Contracts, Alleniom Utilities.
[Normal] EXHIBIT A — POINT OF INTERCONNECTION
[Normal] Feeder ALN-072, 13.2 kV, three-phase. The Company's POI recloser and revenue meter RM-0629 are on the Company's pole at the north lot. The Interconnection Customer's 13.2 kV primary conductors run from the Point of Interconnection to primary switch PSW-1 and step-up transformer T-1 in the equipment yard.
[Normal] EXHIBIT B — FACILITY AND INTERCONNECTION FACILITIES
[Normal] B.1 Generating equipment. Five Vexlar VX-140C inverters, INV-C1 to INV-C5, 140 kW (ac) each at 480 V, three-phase, one on each of canopies C1 to C5; 700 kW (ac) in all. The inverters provide the interconnection protective functions by their certified functions (DIS Table 5-1, Category 2) and operate at the IEEE 1547-2018 Category III default settings and constant power factor 1.00 unless the Company directs otherwise in writing.
[Normal] B.2 Interconnection Customer's interconnection facilities. Inverter ac disconnects AD-C1 to AD-C5, one beside each inverter; PV switchboard SWBD-PV with five 225 A inverter breakers and a 1,200 A main breaker; step-up transformer T-1, 750 kVA, 13.2 kV grounded wye to 480Y/277 V; primary switch PSW-1 with current-limiting fuses; the 13.2 kV primary conductors from PSW-1 to the Point of Interconnection.
[Normal] B.3 Monitoring. The PV monitoring cabinet DAS-1 is the Interconnection Customer's own monitoring and is not part of the Company's telemetry.

[Normal] SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
[Normal] The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
[Normal] Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
[Normal] The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:

 §12.1 Applicability
 This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
 of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
 requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
 in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
 which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
 supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
 engineering standards.

 §12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
 The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
 interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
 classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:

     (a) Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
        MW);
     (b) Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).

 The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
 whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
 processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
 and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.

 Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
 addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
 whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
 Program scope.

 §12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
 A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
 determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
 returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
 cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
 provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.

 §12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
 Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
 Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
 a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
 thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
 active queue without further action of the Company.

 For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
 legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
 federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
 as non-business days and shall not be counted:

   Holiday                                                               Observed Date

   Memorial Day                                                          05/26/2025

   Juneteenth National Independence Day                                  06/19/2025

   Independence Day                                                      07/04/2025

 The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
 verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
 under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
 notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

 §12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
 Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
 customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
 the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
 the date of that written notice.

 For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
 remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
 default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
 deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
 consequences, and different cure paths.

 Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly

 payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
 Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
 issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.

This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.
 §2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:

    (1) Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
    the affected site.
    (2) An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
    on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
    exception).
    (3) The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
    light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.

Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).

§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.

The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.

Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.

The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.

Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.

Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.
 §4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.

Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.

§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.

The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.

Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

POI Recloser Site Acceptance Procedure: PC-SAT-01
   Doc no.                      Rev        Date               Owner
   DPE-PC-SAT-01                Rev 0      07/09/2025         Distribution Protection Engineering

Site: Prairie Corridor Business Park PV (PXA-2024-0343), POI recloser PC-POI-R1 with control NPC-38.
Issued for the site acceptance at cutover under DPS-07 §6.2, against settings sheet DPE-PC-POI-R1 Rev A.
To be performed after installation and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities; results recorded on this form at the test.

Steps
Step 1 Insulation and dielectric. Measure insulation resistance of primary and secondary circuits at 5 kV DC for
one minute; apply the manufacturer's dielectric withstand test to the secondary wiring. Record the values.
Step 2 Instrument transformers. Verify CT ratio 200:5, polarity and burden; verify VT ratio 7200:120 V and
polarity on both sides of the interrupter.
Step 3 Functional testing. Test the elements below against settings sheet Rev A by secondary injection: pickup,
timing and reset for each. Elements: 50/51, 50N/51N, 27, 59, 81U, 81O, 32; 25 and 79 under step 6.
Step 4 End-to-end trip. From each element of step 3, trip the recloser through the interrupter and confirm the
open indication locally and at SCADA.
Step 5 Control, status and metering. Operate the recloser locally and from SCADA; confirm status points and
metering at the SCADA operator display against the RTU point table SCADA-PC-RTU-CFG-01.
Step 6 Synchronism check and reclose logic. With the utility source live and the park bus dead, confirm the 25
element permits the close; close from the control cabinet and confirm the recloser closes. Open the recloser,
open the upstream line disconnect to de-energize the line side, and confirm a close command is refused. Trip
the recloser by secondary injection on the 27 element and confirm it goes to lockout with 79 blocked; confirm
the lockout holds until the operator release. Restore the line side, wait the stable-source time of settings sheet
Rev A (5 minutes), release, and confirm the close through 25.
Step 7 Visible break. Operate the visible-break disconnect; apply the utility padlock in the open position and
confirm the clearance hold.

Acceptance
Accepted in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering on completion of steps 1 to 7 (DPS-07 §6.3).
Prepared: Nolan Achterberg, P.E., Distribution Protection Engineer, 07/09/2025.

RE: Escalation — DER Interconnection Program Delays Affecting Fourteen Municipalities and School
Districts
Dear Ms. Whitcomb:
On behalf of the Alleron Municipal League and the fourteen member communities identified below, I write to
convey our formal and collective concern regarding the continued and, in our view, unreasonable delays
affecting commercial-scale solar interconnection projects currently stalled within Alleniom Utilities’ Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection program. This letter follows repeated informal outreach by individual
member staff to your DER Program Office over the preceding several months, outreach which has not produced
the clarity or the timely progress our members need in order to close out their local capital projects.
The League is writing on behalf of 14 municipalities and school districts across the state of Alleron whose
commercial-scale solar projects — commissioned in good faith with voter-approved bond proceeds, adopted
capital budgets, energy-savings performance contracts, and in several instances state and federal grant awards
remain suspended in your interconnection queue awaiting energization. Among the affected members are:
     Brookfen Unified School District
     City of Elmsworth
     Darnwick Community School District
     Lockmere Community School District
     Cravenwood Community School District
     Town of Tresbay
     City of Marden Falls
     Town of Holcott
Additional League members with projects in the same posture have asked to be represented collectively through
this correspondence and are prepared to be identified upon request. Every one of these projects has been
reviewed and approved by the applicable local governing body, financed through public procurement, and
constructed by licensed contractors under permits issued by the relevant authority having jurisdiction.
The projects at issue are not speculative or exploratory. They range in size from approximately 500 kW to nearly
1 MW and are installed at public schools, municipal water and wastewater treatment plants, community centers,
public libraries, and other municipal facilities. In the great majority of cases construction is complete, mechanical
and electrical inspections have been closed out by local inspectors, and equipment has been standing
energized-ready — in some instances for a period now measured in months — pending only the Company’s
authorization to interconnect and place the systems into commercial operation. Each additional month of delay
defers budgeted operating savings, extends the payback horizon presented to our members’ councils and school
boards, and in the case of grant-funded projects places committed public funding at direct risk of forfeiture.
Our members are patient partners. They understand that the interconnection of distributed generation on the
Company’s distribution system requires careful technical review and, at times, coordination with equipment
procurement, feeder studies, and protection-scheme confirmation. They are willing to meet reasonable technical
requirements. What they are not able to accept — and what this League cannot accept on their behalf — is an
 extended period of silence, shifting explanations, and open-ended hold status without a clear articulation of what
is required, by whom, and by when.
Accordingly, and in a spirit of continued cooperation, the League respectfully requests the following from
Alleniom Utilities:
1. A full accounting of current queue status. For each identified League-member project, please provide the
    project’s assigned application number, current queue position, and complete processing history to date.
2. Hold reasons. For every project currently in a hold, pending, or suspended posture, please identify the
    specific reason for the hold, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to
    release the hold, and the date the hold was established.
3. Expected energization dates. For each project, please provide the Company’s current best estimate of the
    date on which Permission to Operate will be issued, together with any intermediate milestone dates
    (studies, equipment delivery, witness testing, or telemetry acceptance) that inform that estimate.
4. A written response. We request the Company’s response in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the
    League’s Cordwyn office, within a reasonable period consistent with the urgency our members’ councils
    and school boards are attaching to this matter.
5. A meeting. We request an in-person meeting between the Company’s senior distribution leadership, the
    League’s executive office, and designated representatives of the affected members, to be scheduled at the
    Company’s offices in Halston or at a mutually convenient location in Cordwyn at the Company’s preference.
    The League is prepared to convene our members on short notice once the Company proposes a date.
For your awareness, a copy of this letter has been provided to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC),
Energy Resources Division, for the Division’s information. The League has taken this step not as a matter of
confrontation but out of a good-faith obligation to keep the Commission’s staff apprised of a program-level
concern affecting a substantial number of Alleron public entities across multiple service territories within the
Company’s distribution footprint. It remains our strong preference to resolve this matter directly with Alleniom
Utilities.
The League and its members recognize that Alleniom Utilities has been a constructive counterparty on many
prior initiatives, and we approach this escalation with the expectation that the Company shares our interest in
restoring predictable, transparent processing timelines to the DER program. Our members’ communities have
invested public funds, published expected in-service dates to their constituents, and in several cases entered
into contractual arrangements predicated on interconnection occurring by dates that are now past. The credibility
of local government energy planning across Alleron is meaningfully bound up in the outcome, and we are
confident the Company understands the seriousness with which we, our elected officials, and our school boards
regard it.
I would be grateful for the courtesy of an acknowledgment of receipt at your earliest convenience, and I remain
available to discuss any aspect of the foregoing at the telephone number above. Thank you for your prompt
attention to this matter.

Respectfully submitted,
