Dear Ms. Ngoyi:

The Energy Resources Division of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC) is in receipt of
correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:
AML-2025-0620-DER), copied to the Division, escalating on behalf of fourteen member municipalities
and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.

The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.

1. Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:

   a. The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
      application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
      current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.
    b.     The count and identity of all applications currently on on-hold, pending-customer,
        pending-standards, or suspended status, together with the specific hold reason of record for
        each, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to release the
        hold, and the date the hold was established.
   c. The count and identity of all applications for which one or more study or processing timelines
      established under the Company's filed interconnection tariff, procedures, or executed study
      agreements have been exceeded as of the reporting date, together with the timeline of record, the
      actual elapsed time, and the current cause of the overrun.
   d. The count and identity of all applications withdrawn — whether by written applicant request, by
      application of the tariff's deemed-withdrawal provision, or otherwise — during the twelve
      months preceding the reporting date, together with the effective date of each withdrawal and the
      recorded basis for it.
   e.     The count and identity of all formal Notices of Impending Withdrawal, Notices of
        Cancellation, or equivalent written notices issued by the Company to applicants during the
        twelve months preceding the reporting date, together with the notice date, the date sent, the
        method of service, the response deadline computed under the tariff, and the current disposition
        (response received / no response / deemed withdrawn / other).
Where any of the foregoing counts is materially affected by data-integrity items known to the Company
(for example, timing differences, reconciliation items, or other known data-quality issues), the Company is
requested to identify those items and provide the counts both as they presently appear in the Company's
queue records and as the Company understands the underlying facts to be.

2. Backlog-cause summary.
The Company is further requested to provide a written summary describing, in the Company's own
characterization, the principal causes of the current backlog in the commercial DER interconnection
program. The summary should address at a minimum: application volume relative to processing
capacity; the availability and lead time of utility-owned equipment required for energization (including
but not limited to RTU and protection equipment); the status of any internal standards reconciliation
activity affecting screening or protection determinations; the sufficiency of certified-equipment
references relied upon by the Company; the sufficiency of hosting-capacity information made available
to prospective applicants; and any other factors the Company identifies as materially contributing to the
current queue posture. Supporting quantitative material (equipment delivery schedules, staffing
utilization, study cycle times, and the like) is welcome and, where practicable, requested.

3. Format and timing.
Responses should be provided in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the Division's Cordwyn
office, with electronic copies to the docket. Line-item responses under Item 1 above may be provided
by workbook attachment provided each attachment is unambiguously cross-referenced to the
corresponding item. Responses should be received by the Division sufficiently in advance of the
09/10/2025 briefing to allow the Division adequate review; the Division requests that the Company
provide its response no later than 08/22/2025, and, where any portion of the response cannot be
furnished by that date, that the Company so advise the Division in writing no later than 08/08/2025 with
an explanation and a proposed alternative date.

4. Continuing dialogue.
 This request is issued in the ordinary course of the Division's monitoring of interconnection program
performance under the Company's APUC-filed tariff. The Division has no present view as to the merits
of the underlying matter and takes no position on the specific project-level concerns raised in the
League's 06/20/2025 letter, which remain properly a matter between the League's member entities and
the Company in the first instance. The Division's interest at this stage is limited to the queue accounting
and backlog-cause information described above, together with the Company's plan for restoring
predictable processing to the program. The Division remains available to discuss scope, format, or
timing questions at Company request.

The Division appreciates the Company's continued cooperation and looks forward to the Company's
response.

Sincerely,

                                                                   Operations



 Document Control
 Supersedes: none (initial issue).
 Review cycle: annual, or on material change to supplier lead times or operating criticality categories.
 Approving authority: VP, Distribution Operations.
 Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group; System Operations Center
 (SOC); Standards Engineering; Supply Chain — Distribution Equipment.

 §1 SCOPE
 This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
 completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
 Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
 when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
 equipped in a given deployment window.

 This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
 interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
 administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
 those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
 application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
 construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.

 Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
 the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
 Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
 §12.2.

 §2 COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
 As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
 consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
 A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
 request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
 expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
 site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
 emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
 Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
 substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline                                                 Page 1
  Factor definitions:

   •   Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
       a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
       service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
       evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
       designation on the interconnection application.
   •   Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
       date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
       instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
       customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
       fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
   •   Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
       was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
       the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
       verification, controls.
   •   Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
       only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
 External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
 received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
 evidenced by the source documents in §3.

 §3 DOCUMENTATION
 For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
 every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
 of record:

   •   Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
   •   Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
   •   Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
   •   Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
       (Standards Engineering).
   •   Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
   •   Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
       attached by reference (customer submission).
   •   Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
       reference (application file).
   •   Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
 The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
 ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
 the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
 the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.




OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline                                                   Page 2
  Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
 documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
 addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.

 §4 VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
 Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current
 approved suppliers of RTUs and POI reclosers with the following expectations:

   •   Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery
       date, and delivery quantity per device type, retained in the equipment-planning file. Any change to a
       previously committed date or quantity is to be flagged in writing on receipt.
   •   Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets
       required to satisfy the sites eligible under §1 for the current deployment window plus the next
       scheduled delivery window. Expedite requests shall be pursued where a delivery-date change would
       displace a rank-(1) or rank-(2) site.
   •   Alternate sourcing. Where committed lead times exceed the interval between deliveries, Supply
       Chain shall document the shortcoming of the current approved suppliers and evaluate qualification of
       additional vendors under Standards Engineering's certification procedures. Qualification effort shall
       not condition or delay deployment decisions for the current window.
   •   Substitution. Any proposed substitution of device model or configuration relative to the site's
       approved specification is routed to Standards Engineering; substitutions are not accepted on
       schedule pressure alone.
   •   Escrow / spares. A minimum spare quantity per device type shall be held at the operations
       warehouse, replenished on drawdown, and not consumed to accelerate a lower-ranked site ahead of
       a higher-ranked site whose device set is en route.
 Vendor engagement records are subject to audit by Regulatory Affairs on request.

 §5 COORDINATION WITH THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS CENTER
 The ranked deployment list issued under §3 is transmitted to the SOC concurrent with its issuance.
 Coordination steps are as follows:

   •   Pre-deployment briefing. For each device set scheduled to arrive in the deployment window, the
       DER Program Office and the SOC Shift Supervisor confirm the receiving site, the anticipated
       field-installation window, the commissioning sequence, and the telemetry integration steps required
       for permission-to-operate (PTO). Nothing in this guideline modifies the SOC's PTO gating criteria;
       TCS-02 §5 requires utility-owned RTU and SCADA telemetry with live telemetry established prior to
       PTO for sites at or above 500 kW, and this guideline does not authorize interim or provisional
       energization ahead of that condition.
   •   Change control. A change to the ranked list after transmittal to the SOC — for example, arrival of a
       new rank-(1) site, or documented lapse of a committed deadline previously credited at rank (2) — is
       issued by written addendum jointly to Supply Chain and to the SOC. Verbal reprioritization is not to be
       relied upon.
   •   Field constraints. Where feeder condition, crew availability, or outage-window constraints prevent
       installation at a higher-ranked site within the window, the SOC records the constraint and the DER
       Program Office reissues the deployment assignment for that device set to the next-eligible site; the



OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline                                                Page 3
        higher-ranked site retains its rank for the following window.
   •   Commissioning readiness. The SOC's PTO-hold log continues to govern which completed sites are
       eligible for energization steps; sites without established telemetry remain on the hold log until the
       utility-owned RTU is installed and telemetry is verified in accordance with TCS-02.
   •   Reporting. A written record of device-set assignments, installation dates, commissioning outcomes,
       and any addenda issued during the window is retained by the DER Program Office and made
       available to Regulatory Affairs and to the SOC on request.

   SRP-3               Rev 3         02/10/2025               Alleniom Standards Engineering

   Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
   Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;

   §1 Purpose
   This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
   interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
   Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
   be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
   which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.

   Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
   against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
   impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
   judgment.

   Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
   requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.

   §2 Scope
   This procedure applies to:
   (a) all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
   supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and

core: Alleniom Standards Engineering  2024-09-12 09:05:00+00:00 2024-09-13 04:05:00+00:00 Alleniom Standards Engineering   
[Normal] Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
[Normal] 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
[Normal] Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office
[Normal] Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
[Normal] Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
[Normal] Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
[Normal] Owner:  DER Program Office.
[Normal] Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.
[Normal] §1  Purpose
[Normal] This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
[Normal] (a)	applications are closed only on a documented basis;
[Normal] (b)	queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
[Normal] (c)	staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
[Normal] (d)	the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
[Normal] Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
[Normal] §2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
[Normal] A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
[Normal] §2.1  Scope of §2
[Normal] This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
[Normal] (a)	the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
[Normal] (b)	the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
[Normal] (c)	a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
[Normal] §2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
[Normal] To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
[Normal] (a)	be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
[Normal] (b)	be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
[Normal] (c)	identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
[Normal] (d)	state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
[Normal] Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
[Normal] §2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
[Normal] Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
[Normal] 1.	Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
[Normal] 2.	Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
[Normal] 3.	Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
[Normal] 4.	On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
[Normal] 5.	Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
[Normal] Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
[Normal] §2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
[Normal] Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
[Normal] (a)	The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
[Normal] (b)	The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
[Normal] (c)	The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
[Normal] (d)	Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
[Normal] §2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
[Normal] Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
[Normal] §3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
[Normal] Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
[Normal] §3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
[Normal] This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
[Normal] §3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
[Normal] The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
[Normal] (a)	the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
[Normal] (b)	at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
[Normal] (c)	the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
[Normal] §3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
[Normal] Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
[Normal] (a)	be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
[Normal] (b)	be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
[Normal] (c)	identify the application by identifier and site;
[Normal] (d)	state the item(s) requiring response;
[Normal] (e)	state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
[Normal] (f)	state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
[Normal] §3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
[Normal] For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
[Normal] (a)	“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
[Normal] (b)	Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
[Normal] (c)	The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
[TABLE]
  | Holiday | Observed Date
  | Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
  | Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
  | Independence Day | 07/04/2025
[Normal] (d)	Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
[Normal] §3.5  Effect of Non-Response
[Normal] If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
[Normal] (a)	mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
[Normal] (b)	record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
[Normal] (c)	preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.

[Normal] This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
  | Substation | Elderpine
[List Bullet] (c) TCS-02 — Telemetry and Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021); and
[Normal] ARTICLE 5 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
[Normal] 5.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer shall install, at its cost, provisions for a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and shall make available all analog and binary status DNP3 points required by the Company's Telemetry and Communications Standard, together with such communication paths and standing-power provisions as the Company requires for SCADA integration.
[Normal] 5.3 Commissioning of monitoring and control. Satisfactory commissioning and continuous availability of the telemetry described in Section 5.2 are conditions precedent to Permission to Operate. The Facility shall not be paralleled with the Company's distribution system in the absence of live utility telemetry, and any loss of telemetry after Permission to Operate shall be reported and remediated as provided in TCS-02.
[Normal] 5.4 Data and access rights. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company such rights of access to the Facility, and such rights to receive and use metering and telemetry data, as are necessary for the Company to discharge its obligations under the Tariff and applicable Standards.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor, Cm
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
import datetime

DOCNO = "DPO-PTO-0629-01"
NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
GREY = RGBColor(0x55, 0x55, 0x55)

doc = Document()

# ---------- page setup ----------
for s in doc.sections:
    s.page_width = Inches(8.5)
    s.page_height = Inches(11)
    s.left_margin = s.right_margin = Inches(1)
    s.top_margin = Inches(0.9)
    s.bottom_margin = Inches(0.9)

# ---------- styles ----------
st = doc.styles["Normal"]
st.font.name = "Calibri"
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
st.font.size = Pt(10.5)
st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
st.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08

for name, size, before, after in (("Heading 1", 12, 12, 4), ("Heading 2", 11, 9, 3)):
    h = doc.styles[name]
    h.font.name = "Calibri"
    h.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:ascii"), "Calibri")
    h.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:hAnsi"), "Calibri")
    h.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
    h.font.size = Pt(size)
    h.font.bold = True
    h.font.italic = False
    h.font.color.rgb = NAVY
    h.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    h.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    h.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

lb = doc.styles["List Bullet"]
lb.font.name = "Calibri"
lb.font.size = Pt(10.5)
lb.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)


# ---------- helpers ----------
def set_cell_shading(cell, hex_fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hex_fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def set_cell_margins(table, top=60, bottom=60, left=90, right=90):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for k, v in (("top", top), ("left", left), ("bottom", bottom), ("right", right)):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{k}")
        e.set(qn("w:w"), str(v))
        e.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(e)
    tblPr.append(mar)


def remove_borders(table):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    for b in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{b}")
        e.set(qn("w:val"), "nil")
        borders.append(e)
    tblPr.append(borders)


def para_border_bottom(p, size=8, color="1F3A5F", space=1):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    bottom = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    bottom.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    bottom.set(qn("w:sz"), str(size))
    bottom.set(qn("w:space"), str(space))
    bottom.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    pbdr.append(bottom)
    pPr.append(pbdr)


def add_runs(p, parts, size=None):
    """parts: list of str or (str, dict) with keys b, i, color"""
    for part in parts:
        if isinstance(part, str):
            r = p.add_run(part)
            fmt = {}
        else:
            r = p.add_run(part[0])
            fmt = part[1]
        if fmt.get("b"):
            r.bold = True
        if fmt.get("i"):
            r.italic = True
        if fmt.get("color"):
            r.font.color.rgb = fmt["color"]
        if size or fmt.get("size"):
            r.font.size = Pt(fmt.get("size", size))
    return p


def P(parts, style=None, size=None, align=None, after=None, before=None, keep=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else doc.add_paragraph()
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [parts]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def B(parts, size=None):
    return P(parts, style="List Bullet", size=size)


def cell_text(cell, parts, size=9.5, bold=False, align=None):
    cell.text = ""
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [(parts, {"b": bold})] if bold else [parts]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.TOP
    return p


def cell_add_para(cell, parts, size=9.5):
    p = cell.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [parts]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size)
    return p


def set_col_widths(table, widths_in):
    table.autofit = False
    tbl = table._tbl
    tblPr = tbl.tblPr
    layout = OxmlElement("w:tblLayout")
    layout.set(qn("w:type"), "fixed")
    tblPr.append(layout)
    grid = tbl.tblGrid
    for i, gc in enumerate(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(widths_in[i] * 1440)))
    for row in table.rows:
        for i, c in enumerate(row.cells):
            c.width = Inches(widths_in[i])


def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    e = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader")
    e.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(e)


def no_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    e = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit")
    e.set(qn("w:val"), "true")
    trPr.append(e)


def add_field(run, instr):
    f1 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f1.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
    it = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); it.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve"); it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f2.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "separate")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t"); t.text = "1"
    f3 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f3.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
    for el in (f1, it, f2, t, f3):
        run._r.append(el)


# ---------- footer ----------
sec = doc.sections[0]
fp = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
r = fp.add_run(f"{DOCNO} · Rev 0 · 07/14/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · Internal · Page ")
r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
r2 = fp.add_run(); r2.font.size = Pt(8); r2.font.color.rgb = GREY; add_field(r2, "PAGE")
r3 = fp.add_run(" of "); r3.font.size = Pt(8); r3.font.color.rgb = GREY
r4 = fp.add_run(); r4.font.size = Pt(8); r4.font.color.rgb = GREY; add_field(r4, "NUMPAGES")

# ---------- letterhead ----------
p = P([("ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE", {"b": True, "color": NAVY, "size": 14})], after=0)
p = P([("4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com", {"color": GREY, "size": 9})], after=8)
para_border_bottom(p, size=12)

P([("INTERNAL MEMORANDUM", {"b": True, "size": 12, "color": NAVY})], before=4, after=4)

ctl = doc.add_table(rows=4, cols=2)
ctl.style = "Table Grid"
ctl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
for i, (k, v) in enumerate((("Doc no.", DOCNO), ("Rev", "0"), ("Date", "07/14/2025"),
                            ("Owner", "DER Program Office — Engineering Review"))):
    cell_text(ctl.cell(i, 0), k, size=9, bold=True)
    set_cell_shading(ctl.cell(i, 0), "E8EDF3")
    cell_text(ctl.cell(i, 1), v, size=9)
set_col_widths(ctl, [1.0, 3.2])
set_cell_margins(ctl, 30, 30, 80, 80)

P("", after=2)

hdr = doc.add_table(rows=5, cols=2)
remove_borders(hdr)
rows = (
    ("TO:", "Lena Kovalchuk, SOC Shift Supervisor, System Operations Center"),
    ("CC:", "S. Rennick, Commissioning, DER Program Office · Marcus Deele, SCADA/EMS Engineering · "
            "DER Program Office — Contracts · Distribution Operations · DER Program Manager"),
    ("FROM:", "Reviewing Engineer, P.E., DER Program Office"),
    ("DATE:", "07/14/2025"),
    ("SUBJECT:", "Corwyn Office Complex PV (PXA-2023-0629), feeder ALN-072: Permission to Operate "
                 "requested by Corwyn Realty Partners for 08/04/2025"),
)
for i, (k, v) in enumerate(rows):
    cell_text(hdr.cell(i, 0), k, size=10.5, bold=True)
    cell_text(hdr.cell(i, 1), [(v, {"b": k == "SUBJECT:"})], size=10.5)
set_col_widths(hdr, [0.95, 5.55])
set_cell_margins(hdr, 20, 20, 0, 60)

p = P("", after=6)
para_border_bottom(p, size=8)

# ---------- 1. Answer ----------
doc.add_heading("1. Answer", level=1)

P([("Permission to Operate cannot issue on 08/04/2025. Please hold it.", {"b": True, "size": 11.5})], after=6)

P("The site cannot meet the telemetry condition for Permission to Operate (TCS-02 §5; ISA §6.2 and §7.2) "
  "as it is built and as its ISA stands. At this site, everything the Company’s RTU depends on is energized "
  "only through the POI recloser. The RTU’s station supply is taken from Corwyn’s PV switchboard. The five "
  "inverters that supply the per-inverter points draw their control power from their own ac output. The ISA "
  "keeps the recloser open at all times before Permission to Operate except for the witness test (ISA §6.1), "
  "and the recloser has been open since 15:35 on 07/08/2025. While it is open, the RTU has only its UPS and the "
  "inverters cannot answer at all. So there is no moment before Permission to Operate at which the SOC could "
  "find every required point valid, as TCS-02 §5(c) requires. The SOC confirmation entered on the commissioning "
  "checklist for 07/08/2025 was given on the witness-test day, while the recloser was closed. It cannot be "
  "carried forward.")

P("Clearing this needs two things: new construction by Corwyn Realty Partners under a new City of Wrenford "
  "permit, and a written amendment to the ISA signed by both parties. Nothing on the record shows either "
  "begun, and Corwyn has not yet been told. The Office does not expect them to be complete by 08/04/2025 and "
  "cannot give you a substitute date; the earliest date is set by item 1 below. There is no interim or "
  "conditional route: TCS-02 §5 has none.")

P("Leaving aside the four matters under separate review (section 4), nothing else on the record stands in the "
  "way. The witness test, the City’s final approval, the revenue meter and the equipment listing are in order. "
  "When the steps in section 5 are complete, the Office will tell you in writing. Permission to Operate then "
  "issues only on the TCS-02 §5 confirmation of the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift, given at the moment of issue.")

# ---------- 2. Summary table ----------
doc.add_heading("2. What stands in the way: summary", level=1)

t = doc.add_table(rows=4, cols=5)
t.style = "Table Grid"
heads = ["#", "What stands in the way", "Rests on", "Who has to act", "Before 08/04/2025?"]
for i, h in enumerate(heads):
    cell_text(t.cell(0, i), h, size=9, bold=True)
    set_cell_shading(t.cell(0, i), "1F3A5F")
    for r_ in t.cell(0, i).paragraphs[0].runs:
        r_.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
repeat_header(t.rows[0])
data = [
    ("1",
     "The RTU’s station supply is taken from the Facility side of the POI recloser, so the RTU is dark whenever "
     "the recloser is open. The stated UPS endurance is also unproven.",
     "TCS-02 §3.1, §3.4, §4.3, §5; DIS-01 §6; ISA §4.1, §5.2, §6.2, §6.3, §7.2, §8.3–§8.4",

]
for ri, row in enumerate(data, start=1):
    for ci, val in enumerate(row):
        cell_text(t.cell(ri, ci), [(val, {"b": ci in (0, 4)})], size=9)
    no_split(t.rows[ri])
set_col_widths(t, [0.3, 2.05, 1.35, 1.75, 1.05])
set_cell_margins(t, 50, 50, 70, 70)

# ---------- 3. Detail ----------
doc.add_heading("3. The items in detail", level=1)

# Item 1
doc.add_heading("3.1 Item 1: the RTU’s station supply is taken from the Facility side of the POI recloser", level=2)

P([("What it is. ", {"b": True}),
   "Corwyn’s contractor supplies the RTU enclosure on the POI pole from auxiliary panel PP-1, circuit 1. "
   "This is a dedicated 20 A circuit through a 1.5 kVA online UPS in the enclosure, stated as “5.5 h at the RTU "
   "load”. PP-1 is fed by auxiliary transformer TX-1, and TX-1 by a 40 A breaker in the PV switchboard SWBD-PV. "
   "SWBD-PV in turn is fed from the POI recloser through its own main breaker, step-up transformer T-1 and "
   "primary switch PSW-1 (Equipment Schedule, drawing E-101 Rev C; ISA Exhibit A). The RTU therefore has a "
   "mains supply only while the recloser, PSW-1, the SWBD-PV main and the TX-1 breaker are all closed. In "
   "every other state it runs on its UPS and then goes dark. Those states include the whole period before "
   "Permission to Operate (ISA §6.1), any trip to lockout (DPS-07 §5.1(b)), any time the Company keeps the "
   "Facility off (ISA §8.3) and any clearance on the Facility’s disconnects (ISA §8.5). The record shows no "
   "supply to the RTU since the recloser was opened at 15:35 on 07/08/2025 (witness test record WT-0629-01). "
   "On the contractor’s own 5.5-hour figure, the RTU went dark at about 21:05 that evening. The SCADA display "
   "should be showing the Corwyn points as communications-lost; please check."])

P("A supply that does not depend on the recloser is available on site. Corwyn’s own monitoring cabinet DAS-1, "
  "which is not part of the Company’s telemetry (ISA Exhibit B.3), is fed from office-building panel LP-2, "
  "circuit 14 (Monitoring and Communications Schedule, drawing E-401 Rev C). Of the two, the Company’s RTU has "

P("The stated UPS endurance is also unproven. Suppose the unit is the Corvane OL-1500R, the 1.5 kVA online unit "
  "whose data sheet is on file. On its published runtime table, 5.5 h corresponds to a load of only about 25 W. "
  "SCADA/EMS Engineering’s own figures for its standard enclosure kit at another site are a YOT-8963 RTU at "
  "38 W and a cellular modem at 12 W (SCADA-PC-RTU-DWG-01). At that load the same table gives 3.9 h on a new "
  "battery at 25 °C. After the data sheet’s 20% derating for end of battery life and for temperatures below "
  "10 °C, it gives about 3.1 h. This site will see those temperatures: its design low is −24 °C (drawing "

P([("What it rests on. ", {"b": True}),
   "TCS-02 §3.1: the customer provides the station AC service specified in the utility’s site-specific RTU "
   "installation drawing. TCS-02 §3.4: a dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply of at "
   "least 4 hours, “sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages”. That wording "
   "assumes a supply that is normally present, with the UPS bridging short interruptions. This supply is absent "
   "for as long as the recloser is open. TCS-02 §4.3: the telemetry path is designed for 99.5% monthly "
   "availability, and persistent loss of telemetry is a departure from the interconnection basis. TCS-02 §5 and "
   "DIS-01 §6: live telemetry is a condition of Permission to Operate. ISA §4.1: the Facility conforms to "
   "TCS-02. ISA §5.2 and §7.2: Corwyn provides, at its cost, the station service and the other provisions for "
   "the RTU. ISA §6.3 and DPS-07 §6.3: the first parallel operation is observed with the recloser under SCADA "
   "supervision. ISA §8.3 and §8.4: the Company may keep the Facility off on loss of telemetry, and "
   "reconnection is only on the SOC’s release. As built, the RTU is dark in exactly the condition in which the "
   "SOC most needs it: recloser open, waiting to see the source restored and to release reconnection."])

P([("What has to be done, and by whom.", {"b": True})], after=2, keep=True)
B([("Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company: ", {"b": True}),
   "supply the RTU enclosure from a source that is live whenever the feeder is live and does not depend on the "
   "POI recloser or the Facility. One example is a dedicated 120 V branch circuit from the office complex’s own "
   "building distribution, which is how DAS-1 is already fed. The supply must pass through a UPS that has been "
   "shown, from the manufacturer’s runtime data at the enclosure’s actual load and after the manufacturer’s "

   "enclosure. This is new electrical work. It needs a City of Wrenford permit, and the City’s final approval "

1. Answer
Permission to Operate cannot issue on 08/04/2025. Please hold it.
The site cannot meet the telemetry condition for Permission to Operate (TCS-02 §5; ISA §6.2 and §7.2)
as it is built and as its ISA stands. At this site, the RTU’s station supply and the per-inverter data it must
present are both energized only through the POI recloser. The RTU’s station supply is taken from
Corwyn’s PV switchboard, and the five inverters draw their control power from their own ac output. The
ISA keeps the recloser open at all times before Permission to Operate except for the witness test (ISA
§6.1), and the recloser has been open since 15:35 on 07/08/2025. While it is open, the RTU has only its
UPS and the inverters cannot answer at all. So there is no moment before Permission to Operate at
which the SOC could find every required point valid, as TCS-02 §5(c) requires. The SOC confirmation
entered on the commissioning checklist for 07/08/2025 was given on the witness-test day, when the RTU
had power only because the recloser had been closed for the test. It cannot be carried forward.
Clearing this needs two things: new construction by Corwyn Realty Partners under a new City of
Wrenford permit, and a written amendment to the ISA signed by both parties. Nothing on the record
shows either begun, or that Corwyn has been told. The Office does not expect them to be complete by
08/04/2025 and cannot give you a substitute date; the earliest date is set by item 1 below. There is no
interim or conditional route: TCS-02 §5 has none.
Leaving aside the four matters under separate review (section 4), nothing else on the record stands in the
way. The witness test, the City’s final approval, the revenue meter and the equipment listing are in order.
When the steps in section 5 are complete, the Office will tell you in writing. Permission to Operate then
issues only on the TCS-02 §5 confirmation of the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift, given at the moment of
issue.

3. The items in detail
3.1 Item 1: the RTU’s station supply is taken from the Facility side of the POI recloser
What it is. Corwyn’s contractor supplies the RTU enclosure on the POI pole from auxiliary panel PP-1,
circuit 1. This is a dedicated 20 A circuit through a 1.5 kVA online UPS in the enclosure, stated as “5.5 h
at the RTU load”. PP-1 is fed by auxiliary transformer TX-1, and TX-1 by a 40 A breaker in the PV
switchboard SWBD-PV. SWBD-PV in turn is fed from the POI recloser through its own main breaker,
step-up transformer T-1 and primary switch PSW-1 (Equipment Schedule, drawing E-101 Rev C; ISA
Exhibit A). The RTU therefore has a mains supply only while the recloser, PSW-1, the SWBD-PV main
and the TX-1 breaker are all closed. In every other state it runs on its UPS and then goes dark. Those
states include the whole period before Permission to Operate (ISA §6.1), any trip to lockout (DPS-07
§5.1(b)), any time the Company keeps the Facility off (ISA §8.3) and any clearance that opens PSW-1 or
the SWBD-PV main (ISA §8.5). On the record, the RTU has had no mains supply since the recloser was
opened at 15:35 on 07/08/2025 (witness test record WT-0629-01). On the contractor’s own 5.5-hour
figure, it would have gone dark at about 21:05 that evening. The SCADA display should be showing the
Corwyn points as communications-lost; please check.
A supply that does not depend on the recloser is available on site. Corwyn’s own monitoring cabinet
DAS-1, which is not part of the Company’s telemetry (ISA Exhibit B.3), is fed from office-building panel
LP-2, circuit 14 (Monitoring and Communications Schedule, drawing E-401 Rev C). Of the two, the
Company’s RTU has the less secure supply.
The stated UPS endurance is also unproven. If the unit is the Corvane OL-1500R, the 1.5 kVA online unit
whose data sheet is on file, 5.5 h on its published runtime table corresponds to a load of only about 25 W.
SCADA/EMS Engineering’s own figures for its standard enclosure kit at another site are a YOT-8963 RTU
at 38 W and a cellular modem at 12 W (SCADA-PC-RTU-DWG-01). At that load the same table gives 3.9
h on a new battery at 25 °C. After the data sheet’s 20% derating for end of battery life and for
temperatures below 10 °C, it gives about 3.1 h. This site will see those temperatures: its design low is −24
°C (drawing E-301 Rev C). TCS-02 §3.4 requires at least 4 hours.
What it rests on. TCS-02 §3.1: the customer provides the station AC service specified in the utility’s site-
specific RTU installation drawing. TCS-02 §3.4: a dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible
supply of at least 4 hours, “sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages”. That


           DPO-PTO-0629-01 · Rev 0 · 07/14/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · Internal · Page 2 of 5
 wording assumes a supply that is normally present, with the UPS bridging short interruptions. This supply
is absent for as long as the recloser is open. TCS-02 §4.3: the telemetry path is designed for 99.5%
monthly availability, and persistent loss of telemetry is a departure from the interconnection basis. TCS-02
§5 and DIS-01 §6: live telemetry is a condition of Permission to Operate. ISA §4.1: the Facility conforms
to TCS-02. ISA §5.2 and §7.2: Corwyn provides, at its cost, the station service and the other provisions
for the RTU. ISA §8.3 and §8.4: the Company may keep the Facility off on loss of telemetry, and
reconnection is only on the SOC’s release. As built, the RTU is dark in exactly the condition in which the
SOC most needs it: recloser open, waiting to see the source restored and to release reconnection.
What has to be done, and by whom.
 Corwyn Realty Partners, through Brantley Electric Company: supply the RTU enclosure from a
  source that is live whenever the feeder is live and does not depend on the POI recloser or the Facility.
  One example is a dedicated 120 V branch circuit from the office complex’s own building distribution,
  which is how DAS-1 is already fed. The supply must pass through a UPS that has been shown, from
  the manufacturer’s runtime data at the enclosure’s actual load and after the manufacturer’s derating,
  to carry the enclosure for at least 4 hours. PP-1 circuit 1 is then disconnected from the enclosure.
  This is new electrical work. It needs a City of Wrenford permit, and the City’s final approval before it is
  energized (permit WEP-25-0317 condition; ISA §6.2).
 SCADA/EMS Engineering (Marcus Deele): specify the new supply point in the site-specific RTU
  installation drawing. That drawing is what TCS-02 §3.1 and ISA §5.2 require Corwyn to build to. Also
  state the enclosure load the UPS must carry, and confirm that the RTU runs from the new supply with
  the recloser open.
 Commissioning (S. Rennick): add a TCS-02 §3.4 station-service line to the commissioning
  checklist, as CX-PC-01 has. Close it only on the City’s approval and the UPS demonstration.
Can it be done before 08/04/2025? No. The work needs a design, a revised SCADA/EMS drawing, a
new City permit, a new run to the POI pole in the north lot, City inspection and final approval, and
SCADA/EMS confirmation. All of that would have to fit into the 15 business days from 07/15/2025 to
08/04/2025, and nothing on the record shows Corwyn has been told. The Office does not expect it by
08/04/2025, and you should not plan on that date.

3.2 Item 2: no way to energize the Facility before Permission to Operate, so the per-inverter
points cannot be valid at the moment of issue
What it is. TCS-02 §6.1 requires gross generation and run/standby/fault status for each inverter block.
TCS-02 §5(c) requires every required point to be valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged bad-quality) at
the moment Permission to Operate is issued. At Corwyn those points come straight from the five inverters
over one RS-485 link to the RTU (link COM-RTU, drawing E-401 Rev C). The inverters draw their control
power from their own ac output terminals (drawing E-101 Rev C). With the Facility de-energized they
cannot answer, and the RTU must flag their points as communications-lost (TCS-02 §6.3). Re-supplying
the RTU under item 1 does not change that. The Facility can be energized before Permission to Operate

the RTU under item 1 does not change that. The Facility can be energized before Permission to Operate
only by closing the recloser. ISA §6.1 allows that solely for the witness test, which is complete. Unlike
ISA-Halbray-Field-Site-3, the Corwyn ISA has no pre-PTO backfeed term. As the ISA stands, there is no
moment at which the SOC could find all the points valid.
What it rests on. TCS-02 §5(c), §6.1 and §6.3; ISA §6.1, §6.2, §7.2 and §12.1. Also the standing note on
the SOC PTO-Hold Log: TCS-02 §5 has no interim provision.
What has to be done, and by whom.
 DER Program Office — Contracts, with Corwyn Realty Partners: amend the ISA by an instrument
  in writing signed by authorized representatives of both parties (ISA §12.1). The amendment would let
  the Company, on Corwyn’s written request, energize the Facility from the feeder before Permission to
  Operate, with the inverters disabled and not in parallel. The executed Halbray ISA already provides
  for this. The amendment changes neither the capacity nor the Point of Interconnection. It is therefore
  an ordinary written change (DIS-01 §7, “other post-execution changes”; ISA §12.2), not a withdrawal
  and reapplication under Tariff §12.6. It is not parallel operation and relaxes nothing in TCS-02 §5. The


          DPO-PTO-0629-01 · Rev 0 · 07/14/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · Internal · Page 3 of 5
     only alternative would be a per-inverter data source that stays live and valid with the Facility dead,
    and the installed inverters cannot provide one.
   Corwyn Realty Partners: sign the amendment and request the energization in writing.
   Distribution Operations: perform the energization under its own switching order, once the
    amendment is executed and item 1 is closed.
   SOC Shift Supervisor on shift: with the Facility energized in this way, confirm every TCS-02 §6
    point valid at the moment of issue.
Can it be done before 08/04/2025? The amendment could be drafted and signed in that time if both
parties act promptly. Permission to Operate would still wait on item 1.

3.3 Item 3: the SOC confirmation on the commissioning checklist is not a TCS-02 §5
confirmation
What it is. Commissioning checklist CX-CW-01 Rev 2 (07/14/2025) records “Telemetry live at the SOC,
confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor (L. Kovalchuk), 07/08/2025”. That was the witness-test day; the
recloser was closed from 08:10 to 15:35 (WT-0629-01). TCS-02 §5 requires confirmation by the SOC
Shift Supervisor on shift at the time Permission to Operate is requested, with all points valid at the
moment it is issued. Corwyn requested Permission to Operate on 07/10/2025, after the recloser had been
reopened. The other current checklists (CX-PC-01, CX-HB-03, CX-WB-01) correctly hold this item open
until the PTO request. The Corwyn checklist also has no line for the RTU’s station service (TCS-02 §3.4),
which is how item 1 was missed.
What has to be done, and by whom. Commissioning (S. Rennick) revises CX-CW-01 to show the
TCS-02 §5 confirmation as open, to be given at issue, and adds the station-service line from item 1. The
SOC gives the §5 confirmation at issue, and only then.
Can it be done before 08/04/2025? The correction can be made at once. The confirmation itself can only
follow items 1 and 2.

4. What is in order, and what this memo does not cover
The other conditions of ISA §6.2 are met on the record. None of them stands in the way.
 Witness test complete: WT-0629-01, 07/08/2025, under switching order DO-2025-0677, signed by
   the witness engineer (M. Halbrook, P.E.). Every test point on INV-C1 to INV-C5 and on the facility
   passed, and the instruments were within calibration. A witness test was required because the SWBD-
   PV breakers are not carried on CEL-2025-Q2. The test and its record meet ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3
   §4.1 to §4.3.
 Authority having jurisdiction: City of Wrenford Certificate of Final Approval, permit WEP-25-0317,

steps.message:
The memo says Permission to Operate **cannot issue on 08/04/2025** and tells Lena to hold it. It is saved as `/filesystem/Corwyn_PTO_Memo.docx` (5 pages), and I opened one work package, #47, for the site in the DER Program Backlog Review project.

**Why it can't issue.** The ISA keeps the POI recloser open at all times before Permission to Operate, except for the witness test (§6.1). With the recloser open, the site cannot have the live telemetry that TCS-02 §5 requires at the moment of issue:
- **The RTU has no power.** Corwyn feeds it from its own PV switchboard, behind the recloser. The recloser has been open since 15:35 on 07/08, so the RTU has had only its UPS since then. On the contractor's own 5.5-hour figure, it went dark around 21:05 that evening. The memo asks Lena to check her SCADA display for this.
- **The inverters can't report.** They take their control power from their own ac output, so the per-inverter data the RTU must present is also dead.
- **The ISA allows no early energization.** Unlike the Halbray ISA, Corwyn's has no term letting the Company energize the site before Permission to Operate.
- **The SOC confirmation on the checklist doesn't count.** It is dated 07/08, the witness-test day, when the recloser was closed. TCS-02 §5 requires the confirmation when Permission to Operate is requested and issued.

**What has to be done, and by whom:**
- **Corwyn Realty Partners (through Brantley Electric):** power the RTU from a source that doesn't depend on the recloser. Their own monitoring cabinet is already fed that way, from an office-building panel. They must also show the UPS lasts at least 4 hours at the actual load. The 5.5-hour claim isn't supported: on SCADA/EMS's own figures for its standard kit, the UPS would give about 3.1 hours after derating. This is new work needing a City of Wrenford permit and final approval. Not achievable by 08/04.
- **Corwyn and DER Program Office Contracts:** amend the ISA so the site can be energized before Permission to Operate with the inverters disabled. It isn't a capacity or interconnection-point change, so an ordinary written amendment is enough. Without it, the SOC can never confirm telemetry for this site. It could be signed in time, but Permission to Operate would still wait on the RTU supply.
- **SCADA/EMS Engineering:** specify the new supply point in the RTU installation drawing, state the enclosure load, and confirm the RTU runs on the new supply.
- **Distribution Operations:** do the switching for the early energization once the amendment is signed.
- **Commissioning (S. Rennick):** correct the checklist, which has no line for the RTU's power supply.
- **The Office:** reply to Corwyn's 07/10 letter.

Apart from the four matters under separate review, everything else on the record is in order. That covers the witness test, the City's final approval, the revenue meter, and the inverter listing and certificate.

The work package records the determination, the basis, and all of the items above with owners, including Corwyn's two. It is assigned to S. Rennick at High priority, with Lena and Marcus Deele as watchers. Dates are 07/14 to 08/15/2025, matching the other backlog items.

Things I chose that you may want to change:
- The memo's document number (DPO-PTO-0629-01) is my own; nothing on record set one.
- The P.E.'s name, licence number, signature and date are left blank for the reviewing engineer to fill in.
- The UPS check assumes the "1.5 kVA online UPS" is the Corvane OL-1500R, the only such data sheet on file.
